translations.dea81ac60cd5c9f783d27fd1: One at a time: one task per sheet.
translations.de129e4fe29e97c73325d509: The agent sheet brings together the 7 answers, the calculated autonomy level, the ready-to-use instruction, 3 tests, and the supervision checklist. There are two paths. The web Sheet (⟪P0⟫) works in the browser, with presets for 10 areas such as clinic, store, and real estate. The skill /ficha-agente is for people using Claude Code in the terminal (the text command screen). It asks the same interview questions and saves everything into a file ⟪P1⟫.
translations.d97f06878223d8e21d6242d7: The sheet forces you to answer the questions that usually get left for later, such as what to do if data is missing and when the agent stops. The level is not a guess: it comes from a fixed rule that only goes down. And the result already includes an instruction to paste and tests to run.
translations.c7122954955d0126cfbd26f1: Web sheet: in the browser, with presets for 10 areas.
translations.f40943ab8d65e30fc8706358: Skill: /ficha-agente in the Claude Code terminal.
translations.4d50b2cff06ff8551b8850e9: Preset: your area’s ready sheet to adjust.
translations.dac3c69b9e943bd9a97c1288: ⟪P0⟫: file with sheet, instruction, and tests.
translations.d1aa842dcb47a9c1c0f0f817: Every sheet comes with 3 tests before you trust it: missing or contradictory information from the source, a forbidden request, and an alert situation. You run each one and compare it with the expected behavior. If it fails, adjust one rule at a time and run again—so you know which change fixed it.
translations.b338f0cf66e5cd6197a0c340: An agent that passes the easy case can still make up data in the difficult one. The tests simulate exactly the moments when the error becomes costly. Changing one rule at a time prevents the “fix one thing, break another without noticing” effect.
translations.b72b8051553ab2762e6cfffd: Test 1: if data is missing, it doesn’t invent.
translations.d9839b6123755b8b023ebcbe: Test 2: forbidden request; it refuses and calls you.
translations.eef7d04bb1ec8e589494a21f: Test 3: alert; it stops and calls you.
translations.c0b41af96a7d31a8a93966fe: Adjust: one rule at a time, then repeat.
translations.193d787cd8dfb20a6db8ff56: Auditing means evaluating an instruction that already exists (a saved prompt, a ⟪P0⟫, a ⟪P1⟫, or a custom GPT) against the 7 principles. Each principle gets a score of 0 (missing), 1 (vague), or 2 (clear), with the excerpt that proves it. Then you apply the level rule and check whether the current autonomy is above what the rule allows.
translations.84cc2ef91411686bc3d2b078: A lot of people already have agents running without ever checking what they can do. Auditing finds, within minutes, the most common risk: autonomy greater than the task justifies. And it comes with ready-to-paste corrections, without needing to redo everything.
translations.b924f9f5a9096ab3a995986b: Score: 0 missing, 1 vague, 2 clear, with evidence.
translations.27c4e27b2a7b21bd432568df: Level: the rule applied to what the text allows.
translations.52686046348350740b270233: Main finding: autonomy above the rule.
translations.da1715b26e45f189148907a5: Corrections: at most 5, starting with the riskiest one.
translations.88dd64f486c4d8dadb475c5e: Turning on the agent isn’t the end—it’s the start of the trial period. During the first week, you check every day for 2 minutes, log each failure in one line, and at the end of the week adjust a rule. The failure log has dates, what broke, the smallest correction, and the changed sheet rule.
translations.fac7740b50d9d8c25c458084: The most expensive mistakes show up in the first few days, when the instruction encounters real cases you didn’t predict. Short, daily supervision catches these errors early. And the log becomes the proof for leveling up afterward, rather than leveling up based on impression.
translations.7eeacc6c0eaaf0fe57404d88: Promotion: only with clean weeks recorded.
translations.a1cd71183cb635c38cb6d9ac: ⟪P0⟫6⟪P1⟫⟪P2⟫From the sheet to the system: multiple agents, one organization⟪P3⟫
translations.1001cee179bbfa318d30f1a5: With the first agent running, more show up. Then the organization has three parts: people, processes, and agents. An agent map lists each one with its task, level, source of truth, human owner, and who it delivers to. Each agent keeps its own sheet; the map shows how they fit together.
translations.f56d7c3401ab6aaeb001d1a0: Without a map, agents overlap, read different sources for the same data, and no one knows who’s responsible for them. With a map, each agent has an owner and each delivery has a destination. It’s the same logic as the org chart, now including who isn’t a person.
translations.b3810a9e95048c3209e54f82: People: owners who approve and respond.
translations.0644579eae1e6247137c42dc: Processes: the path the work takes.
translations.473028b0315970ac4217ffcf: Agents: each one has its own sheet and level.
translations.cacf639a7f9d4a0f68cae6f7: Map: who does what, with which source and owner.
